title: Pictograms, bar & pie charts
examples: How do I know what the symbols mean on the chart?
What is the difference between a bar chart and a pictogram?
Can I use a pie chart for things that are not parts of a whole?

explain.say: Today we will learn about showing data using pictures and charts. We will look at pictograms, bar charts, and pie charts. These help us see information clearly. Say this with me: pictograms, bar charts, and pie charts.

items: Show data using pictures and charts

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: fractions of a pie. Look at the whole pie, the one slice and the three eighths. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

A pictogram uses pictures to show amounts. Each picture stands for a certain number. You must always look for the key first. The key tells you what one picture equals. For example, if one apple picture means five apples, that is your key.

items: Key tells what one picture equals

explain.say: A bar chart uses rectangular bars to show data. The height or length of the bar shows the amount. The labels tell you what the bars are measuring. For instance, if the blue bar reaches ten, it means ten items were counted.

A pie chart shows parts of a whole circle. The whole circle always represents one hundred percent. Each slice shows a fraction of the total amount. For example, if one slice is one quarter, it is one fourth of the whole.

draw.text: Pie Chart: Parts of a whole circle

faq.q: What is the key in a pictogram?
faq.a: The key explains what one picture symbol represents. It tells you the scale of the chart. You can also ask what the symbols mean or what the scale is.
asks: How do I read the key?
What does this symbol stand for?

faq.q: Can I use a bar chart for anything?
faq.a: Bar charts are great for comparing different groups or categories. You compare the heights of the different bars. You might also ask if I can compare things with a bar chart.
asks: What is a bar chart used for?
Should I use a bar chart here?

faq.q: How do I know if a pie chart is correct?
faq.a: The slices in a pie chart must always add up to a complete circle. The total must equal one hundred percent. You could also ask if the parts make a whole.
asks: Does the pie chart add up to one?

faq.q: What is the difference between a pictogram and a bar chart?
faq.a: A pictogram uses pictures, while a bar chart uses solid bars of different heights. Both show amounts, but they use different visuals. You could ask what the difference is.

faq.q: What do the angles in a pie chart mean?
faq.a: The angles show the proportion of the whole circle that each slice takes. A full circle has three hundred sixty degrees. You might also ask what a full circle is in degrees.
asks: How many degrees is the whole pie?
What does the angle tell me?

facts: A pictogram uses pictures to represent data amounts.
A bar chart compares amounts using the height or length of bars.
A pie chart shows parts that make up a whole circle.
The total angle in a full circle is three hundred sixty degrees.
The key explains the value of one symbol in a pictogram.

quiz.say: If one book picture equals ten books, and you see three pictures, how many books is that?
quiz.why: You multiply the number of pictures by the value given in the key.

wrong.0: This is a common mistake because you might add the numbers together.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you multiplied the key value by itself.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only used the value from the key once.

quiz.say: If a pie chart has a slice that takes up ninety degrees, what fraction of the whole is it?
quiz.why: Ninety degrees is exactly one fourth of the total three hundred sixty degrees.

wrong.0: This is wrong because half of three hundred sixty is one hundred eighty degrees.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you need to find the part, not multiply the angle.
wrong.3: This is tempting because ninety is close to one third of three hundred sixty.

quiz.say: A bar chart compares the number of students who like apples, bananas, and oranges. If the banana bar is twice as high as the apple bar, what does this mean?

options.show: More students like bananas than apples.
options.say: More students like bananas than apples.

options.show: The apples are twice the bananas.
options.say: The apples are twice the bananas.

quiz.why: If one bar is twice the height of another, it means there are twice as many for that item.

wrong.1: This reverses the comparison given in the problem statement.
wrong.2: This confuses comparing two items with finding a total sum.
wrong.3: This ignores the information that one bar is specifically twice the other.
